title: Evidence payload minifier and approval onramp
content:
Purpose
This draft proposes a compact, verifiable evidence payload format plus a low-friction approval onramp for customer-managed networking changes in Private deployments. Goals: reduce per-change telemetry size, make handoff auditable for customers and Redwood, and enable fast automated triage for low-risk updates (canary-friendly).

Background & problem statement
- Private customers (VPC/on-prem) require strong forensic evidence when network changes affect tenant connectivity or inference traffic routing.
- Full audit bundles are often large (pcap/whole-config diffs) and expensive to archive and transfer.
- Current approval flows either force heavy operator involvement or are too permissive for enterprise compliance.
- Need: a graded approach that encodes minimal but sufficient evidence for low-risk changes and an escalation path to full forensic bundles only when required.

Design principles
1) Minimalism first: prefer small structured payloads that capture intent, impact surface, and digest pointers to richer artifacts.
2) Verifiability: every payload must include cryptographic assertions (hashes, signing keys) so parties can detect tampering.
3) Privacy/scope: avoid shipping sensitive customer config secrets inside the payload; use references, short proofs, and selective snapshots.
4) Triageable: payload fields should map to automated risk heuristics allowing immediate accept/deny/followup decisions.
5) Pluggable escalation: lightweight path for auto-approval and clear criteria for promoting to full evidence collection.

Bento evidence format (concept) — 3 parts
- header (small): change id, actor, timestamp, intended scope (CIDR lists or named endpoints), approval policy id, short risk score
- digest-set: canonical hashes of artifacts (config-diff hash, namespace snapshot hash, pre-change telemetry hash) + size metadata + pointer URIs (S3/edge store) when needed
- attestations: operator signature (base64), operator-role, optional customer-side acknowledgement token, optional runtime snapshot signature (kv cache digest)

Example minimal payload (human readable sketch)
- change_id: bento-2025-03-02-8421
- actor: cust-admin@acme.example.com
- scope: subnet-10a (10.0.3.0/24), egress-rule-7
- policy_id: net-policy-minimal-2
- risk_score: 12 (auto-allow threshold 15)
- digests: {cfg_diff: sha256:af3..., snapshot: sha256:7b1..., telemetry_sample: sha256:2c9...}
- artifacts_uri: s3://redwood-evidence/acme/bento-8421/ (may be empty for tiny changes)
- attestation: operator_sig: SIGN(...), customer_ack: TOKEN(...)

Risk heuristics (for auto-onramp)
- auto-allow if: risk_score < 15 AND scope does not include public-exposed rules AND change size < 4KB digest footprint AND no crossover into managed-routing tables.
- escalate to full collection if: risk_score >= 15 OR change touches edge peering or cross-account routes OR artifacts_uri points to large diffs flagged by on-device sampler.

Approval gate model (flows)
1) Fast path (auto): system validates bento payload, verifies signatures, runs heuristics -> auto-allow, emits compact audit record.
2) Soft-approve (human light touch): flagged low-medium risk; sends to operator queue with summarized evidence card (bento header + risk highlights); operator can reject/approve within SLA 1hr.
3) Full review: high-risk or failed auto-verify -> collect full forensic bundle (config diffs, packet-sample, logs), schedule canary, require multi-party sign-off per customer policy.

Operator UX / Onboarding onramp
- A single-page approval card in Console showing: change summary, bento header, one-line risk rationale, quick links to artifacts (if present), buttons: Approve / Reject / Request full bundle.
- Mobile/Slack quick-actions for low-risk approve (tokenized).
- Customer-managed webhook: customers can optionally receive the bento payload and auto-approve locally by returning signed ack tokens (support for webhook retry & clock skew).

Data retention & storage model
- Store compact bento records in primary audit index for 2 years (searchable).
- Full forensic bundles kept per customer SLA (default 90 days) and gated by escalation events; choose cold archival after SLA.
- Store only digests in long-term index; artifacts URIs expire (pre-signed urls) after retention window to avoid leaking customer snapshots.

Security & compliance notes
- Payload signing: use customer key or operator key; accept multiple signatures. Keys are recorded in attestation metadata and checked against KMS thumbprints.
- Avoid PII in payload: any customer-identifying config should be hashed and replaced with stable referents.
- Tamper-evidence: include chain-of-trust header with root-of-trust id for the deployment (for Private, the customer-controlled root can be used).

Observability & metrics (suggested)
- metric.audit.bento.count (by outcome: auto-allowed, soft-approve, escalated)
- metric.audit.bento.latency_ms (from payload submission to final decision)
- metric.audit.forensic_bundle.size_bytes (histogram)
- alert when auto-allow rate >90% and average risk_score >10 (signals potential heuristic drift)

Open questions / trade-offs
- How frequently do customers want to inject their own attestations vs rely on Redwood operator signature?
- Is 2-year compact-index retention acceptable for regulated customers? Offer longer retention as add-on?
- Do we provide a Redwood CLI for on-device bento assembly (recommended) or require customers to assemble server-side?

Implementation plan (phases)
- Phase 0 (MVP, 6w): bento header + digest-set + signature verification; console approval card; auto-allow heuristic prototype; sample telemetry exporter.
- Phase 1 (12w): webhook ack support; artifacts URI storage; operator queue and soft-approve flow; basic metrics & alerts.
- Phase 2 (quarter): full forensic bundle collection, archival policies, customer KMS integration for signatures, SLA controls, docs & runbooks.

Acceptance criteria (MVP)
- Console shows approval card for incoming bento payloads and allows operator actions.
- System can verify signatures and compute risk_score from header/metadata.
- Auto-allow path respects heuristics and records outcome to audit index.
- Linked artifacts (if provided) are retrievable via pre-signed URIs for the retention window.

Next steps & owners
- Product: finalize minimal bento schema (Maya Chen)
- Applied ML/Infra: prototype risk heuristics and sampler (Ethan Park)
- Security: signature & KMS integration plan (Lena Ortiz)
- Eng: spike on small-bundle storage & pre-signed URI lifecycle (Arjun Rao)

Notes to reviewers
- This is intentionally lightweight and experimental; primary goal is to reduce friction for routine tenant network updates while preserving traceability. Feedback: please add corner cases from current onboarding tickets and any compliance red-lines we must hit for EU customers.

Appendix: quick sketch of JSON bento object
{
  "change_id": "bento-2025-03-02-8421",
  "actor": "cust-admin@acme.example.com",
  "scope": ["10.0.3.0/24"],
  "policy_id": "net-policy-minimal-2",
  "risk_score": "12",
  "digests": {"cfg_diff":"sha256:af3...","snapshot":"sha256:7b1..."},
  "artifacts_uri": "s3://redwood-evidence/acme/bento-8421/",
  "attestation": {"operator_sig":"BASE64...","customer_ack":"TOKEN..."}
}

(We will convert the above sketch into a formal Avro/JSON schema in the next iteration.)
